title: A. The Tower is Going Home

legend: On a chessboard with a width of 109$$$10^9$$$ and a height of 109$$$10^9$$$, the rows are numbered from bottom to top from 1$$$1$$$ to 109$$$10^9$$$, and the columns are numbered from left to right from 1$$$1$$$ to 109$$$10^9$$$. Therefore, for each cell of the chessboard you can assign the coordinates (x,y)$$$(x,y)$$$, where x$$$x$$$ is the column number and y$$$y$$$ is the row number.

Every day there are fights between black and white pieces on this board. Today, the black ones won, but at what price? Only the rook survived, and it was driven into the lower left corner — a cell with coordinates (1,1)$$$(1,1)$$$. But it is still happy, because the victory has been won and it's time to celebrate it! In order to do this, the rook needs to go home, namely — on the upper side of the field (that is, in any cell that is in the row with number 109$$$10^9$$$).
Everything would have been fine, but the treacherous white figures put spells on some places of the field before the end of the game. There are two types of spells:
Vertical. Each of these is defined by one number x$$$x$$$. Such spells create an infinite blocking line between the columns x$$$x$$$ and x+1$$$x+1$$$.

Horizontal. Each of these is defined by three numbers x1$$$x_1$$$, x2$$$x_2$$$, y$$$y$$$. Such spells create a blocking segment that passes through the top side of the cells, which are in the row y$$$y$$$ and in columns from x1$$$x_1$$$ to x2$$$x_2$$$ inclusive. The peculiarity of these spells is that it is impossible for a certain pair of such spells to have a common point. Note that horizontal spells can have common points with vertical spells.

Let's recall that the rook is a chess piece that in one move can move to any point that is in the same row or column with its initial position. In our task, the rook can move from the cell (r0,c0)$$$(r_0,c_0)$$$ into the cell (r1,c1)$$$(r_1,c_1)$$$ only under the condition that r1=r0$$$r_1 = r_0$$$ or c1=c0$$$c_1 = c_0$$$ and there is no blocking lines or blocking segments between these cells (For better understanding, look at the samples).

Fortunately, the rook can remove spells, but for this it has to put tremendous efforts, therefore, it wants to remove the minimum possible number of spells in such way, that after this it can return home. Find this number!
input: The first line contains two integers n$$$n$$$ and m$$$m$$$ (0≤n,m≤105$$$0 \le n,m \le 10^5$$$) — the number of vertical and horizontal spells.

Each of the following n$$$n$$$ lines contains one integer x$$$x$$$ (1≤x<109$$$1 \le x  \lt  10^9$$$) — the description of the vertical spell. It will create a blocking line between the columns of x$$$x$$$ and x+1$$$x+1$$$.

Each of the following m$$$m$$$ lines contains three integers x1$$$x_1$$$, x2$$$x_2$$$ and y$$$y$$$ (1≤x1≤x2≤109$$$1 \le x_{1} \le x_{2} \le 10^9$$$, 1≤y<109$$$1 \le y  \lt  10^9$$$) — the numbers that describe the horizontal spell. It will create a blocking segment that passes through the top sides of the cells that are in the row with the number y$$$y$$$, in columns from x1$$$x_1$$$ to x2$$$x_2$$$ inclusive.
It is guaranteed that all spells are different, as well as the fact that for each pair of horizontal spells it is true that the segments that describe them do not have common points.
output: In a single line print one integer — the minimum number of spells the rook needs to remove so it can get from the cell (1,1)$$$(1,1)$$$ to at least one cell in the row with the number 109$$$10^9$$$
note: In the first sample, in order for the rook return home, it is enough to remove the second horizontal spell.

In the second sample, in order for the rook to return home, it is enough to remove the only vertical spell. If we tried to remove just one of the horizontal spells, it would not allow the rook to get home, because it would be blocked from above by one of the remaining horizontal spells (either first one or second one), and to the right it would be blocked by a vertical spell.
In the third sample, we have two horizontal spells that go through the whole field. These spells can not be bypassed, so we need to remove both of them.
In the fourth sample, we have no spells, which means that we do not need to remove anything.
In the fifth example, we can remove the first vertical and third horizontal spells.

legend.ai: 每天这块棋盘上都有黑白棋子之间的战斗。今天，黑方赢了，但付出了什么代价？只有车幸存下来，并且它被逼到了左下角——坐标为 (1,1)$$$(1,1)$$$ 的格子。但它依然很开心，因为胜利已经赢得，是时候庆祝了！为此，车需要回家，也就是——回到棋盘的上边(即任意一个位于编号为 109$$$10^9$$$ 的行中的格子)。
本来一切都会很顺利，但阴险的白方棋子在比赛结束前对棋盘的一些位置施放了咒语。咒语有两种类型：
竖直咒语。每个由单个数字 x$$$x$$$ 定义。此类咒语在第 x$$$x$$$ 列与第 x+1$$$x+1$$$ 列之间创建一条无限长的阻挡线。
水平咒语。每个由三个数字 x1$$$x_1$$$、x2$$$x_2$$$、y$$$y$$$ 定义。此类咒语创建一条阻挡线段，该线段穿过位于第 y$$$y$$$ 行、列号从 x1$$$x_1$$$ 到 x2$$$x_2$$$(含)的单元格的上边界。这些咒语的特殊之处在于，任意两个此类咒语都不可能存在公共点。注意，水平咒语可以与竖直咒语存在公共点。
让我们回顾一下，车是一种棋子，一步可以移动到与其初始位置同一行或同一列的任意位置。在本任务中，车可以从格子 (r0,c0)$$$(r_0,c_0)$$$ 移动到格子 (r1,c1)$$$(r_1,c_1)$$$，仅当满足 r1=r0$$$r_1 = r_0$$$ 或 c1=c0$$$c_1 = c_0$$$，并且这两个格子之间没有阻挡线或阻挡线段时才可以(为了更好地理解，请看样例)。
幸运的是，车可以移除咒语，但为此需要付出巨大的努力，因此它希望移除尽可能少的咒语，使得在这之后它能回到家中。求这个数量！

input.ai: 第一行包含两个整数 n$$$n$$$ 和 m$$$m$$$(0≤n,m≤105$$$0 \le n,m \le 10^5$$$)——竖直咒语和水平咒语的数量。
接下来的 n$$$n$$$ 行中的每一行包含一个整数 x$$$x$$$(1≤x<109$$$1 \le x  \lt  10^9$$$)——对竖直法术的描述。它将在第 x$$$x$$$ 列和第 x+1$$$x+1$$$ 列之间生成一条阻挡线。

接下来的 m$$$m$$$ 行中的每一行包含三个整数 x1$$$x_1$$$、x2$$$x_2$$$ 和 y$$$y$$$(1≤x1≤x2≤109$$$1 \le x_{1} \le x_{2} \le 10^9$$$，1≤y<109$$$1 \le y  \lt  10^9$$$)——描述水平法术的数字。它将在编号为 y$$$y$$$ 的行中、从第 x1$$$x_1$$$ 列到第 x2$$$x_2$$$ 列(包含两端)的单元格的上边穿过，并生成一条阻挡线段。
保证所有法术均不相同，并且对于任意一对水平法术，它们所描述的线段没有公共点。

output.ai: 请在一行中输出一个整数——车需要移除的最少法术数量，使其能够从单元格 (1,1)$$$(1,1)$$$ 到达编号为 109$$$10^9$$$ 的行中的至少一个单元格。

note.ai: 在第一个样例中，为了让车回到家，只需移除第二个水平法术。
在第二个样例中，为了让车回到家，只需移除唯一的竖直法术。如果我们只尝试移除一个横向法术，车仍然无法回到家，因为它的上方会被剩下的横向法术之一（第一个或第二个）挡住，而右侧会被一个竖直法术挡住。
在第三个样例中，有两个横向法术贯穿整个场地。这些法术无法绕过，因此我们需要将它们全部移除。
在第四个样例中，没有任何法术，这意味着我们不需要移除任何东西。
在第五个样例中，我们可以移除第一个竖直法术和第三个横向法术。
